At three in the morning the operations floor was nearly empty, lit only by the blue glow of the monitors. Marcus sat with a cup of cold coffee and watched the new model run load, row by row, onto the map. The storm had shifted. Not by much; maybe forty miles north of where the last run had put it; but forty miles was the difference between a rainy Tuesday and a city under water. He zoomed in on the coastline and checked the pressure field twice. Then he picked up the phone and called the duty officer. "I think we need to issue it now," he said. "Not at six." There was a pause on the line, then a tired voice said, "Send me the graphics." He dragged the files into the folder and hit send.
